plan: This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: bidding higher than value risks paying more than the item is worth if I win against a bid between my value and my bid; bidding lower reduces my chance of winning profitable auctions without changing what I pay if I win. Since my payment only depends on the second-highest bid (not my own bid, as long as I'm highest), truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy, regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding my true value of $6 maximizes my expected profit without risk of overpaying. Bidding below value only reduces my chance of winning without improving my payoff conditional on winning.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. This is because if I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding higher than my value risks overpaying, while bidding lower only risks losing profitable auctions. With no prior round history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid my true value of $17 to maximize expected profit.
